features.behavior: 项目文档可从 docs/README.md 定位产品、架构、开发、测试、进度、决策和功能状态，且不存在旧版重复文档

POST /checkin uses the SpoonOS safety graph: accepted input persists one compliant reflection, while clarify, rejected, and crisis outcomes create no proof and do not advance progress; invalid model output is repaired once then falls back safely.

POST /checkin uses a stable checkinId and persistent SpoonOS checkpoints: after a recoverable node failure, retrying the same request resumes from the last durable node without regenerating completed reflection work or duplicating DailyLog/progress; the response exposes recovery and execution metadata.

Non-demo API access requires a one-time wallet signature session bound to one address, and tx/NFT/milestone confirmations mutate local state only after RPC verification of receipt status, sender, configured contract, chain, and expected event data.

Only a persisted, safety-approved checkin can obtain a short-lived single-use validator signature accepted by ProofRegistry; revoke and supersede append immutable compensation records, invalidate pending approvals, and revoked proofs no longer count toward progress or milestone eligibility.

A repeatable maintenance command removes expired wallet challenges, expired or revoked wallet sessions, expired unused proof approvals, and graph checkpoints beyond status-specific retention windows, while preserving active credentials, recoverable recent checkpoints, consumed approval audit records, and all business logs; dry-run reports the same candidates without mutating data.

NFT image generation accepts only an authenticated owned persisted log reference; the backend builds third-party image prompts exclusively from public task/day visual metadata, never from diary text, Reflection content, wallet address, proof data, or client-supplied prompt fields, and unauthorized or revoked logs cannot generate images.

An authenticated eligible user obtains milestone mint preparation from the backend, including the canonical deterministic tokenId and metadata URI used by receipt verification; the frontend mints exactly those values and no longer invents timestamp-based token IDs, so a valid MilestoneNFT Transfer event can be confirmed and recorded idempotently.

The daily completion path is bound to the exact persisted log shown by the page: checkin, validator approval, verified Proof submission, verified Day NFT mint, and progress refresh complete one idempotent loop without reselecting a different current-day log; an integration test proves the same log reaches SUBMITTED, consumes its approval, records its Day NFT receipt, and appears in completed/minted progress.

Non-demo startup exposes an explicit production readiness gate: /health reports ready=false with named blocking configuration issues when RPC, contract addresses, milestone metadata URI, or validator private key are missing or placeholder values; the frontend config type consumes that status and wallet transaction helpers refuse zero-address contract configuration before asking the wallet to send a transaction.

The frontend has one active backend API seam: src/lib/api/index.ts exports httpClient only; legacy browser-side mock/Agent adapters and old frontend/lib API/ABI modules are deleted, no frontend imports or text references remain, and production build still passes.

A browser-level smoke test proves the demo frontend loop works through the real Next.js UI and one backend seam: with a controlled mock backend, a user can enter a demo identity, open Day 1, submit a meaningful checkin, see the generated reflection, navigate to progress, and see Day 1 recorded without using the deleted mock/Agent adapters.
